questions.q: What does Stephen Key recommend doing with competitors?
a: Partner with them instead of fighting them
Undercut their prices until they quit
Copy their products without giving credit
Sue them to win back market share
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends an if you can't beat them, join them approach, as Hot Picks did with Dunlop.

questions.q: Why is a good manufacturer important when licensing an idea?
a: Your name stands behind the product's quality
Manufacturers handle all the marketing
Cheaper factories mean higher profits
They own the rights to your idea
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that licensing puts your name on the product, so its quality reflects on you.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest getting a top manufacturer's attention?
a: Ask an established ally for a referral
Call the company's chief executive directly
Offer to pay double the normal rate
Post your idea publicly on social media
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests an introduction from a major player to reach their trusted manufacturer.

questions.q: What mistake does Key warn against when creating a follow-up product?
a: Targeting a completely different audience
Making only small improvements
Keeping the same customer base
Offering it at a lower price
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that a follow-up product should serve the same customers or a subset of them.

questions.q: What is the benefit of ideas that improve existing products?
a: The market has already validated them
They require no manufacturer at all
They can never be copied by rivals
They always sell for a premium
questions.why: Lesson 1 says incremental improvements are already validated because people buy similar products.
